'''''Plantago ovata''''', known by many [[common name]]s including '''blond plantain''',<ref name=BSBI07>{{BSBI 2007 |access-date=2014-10-17 }}</ref> '''desert Indianwheat''',<ref>{{citation |url=http://plants.usda.gov/plant-profile?symbol=PLOV |title=USDA PLANTS |access-date=10 June 2016}}</ref> '''blond psyllium''',<ref name=GRIN>{{citation |url=https://npgsweb.ars-grin.gov/gringlobal/taxonomydetail.aspx?id=28790 |title=USDA GRIN Taxonomy |access-date=10 June 2016}}</ref> and '''isabghol''',<ref name=GRIN/> is native to the Mediterranean region and naturalized in central, eastern, and south Asia and North America.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Plantago ovata in Flora of China @ efloras.org|url=http://www.efloras.org/florataxon.aspx?flora_id=2&taxon_id=250095355|access-date=2020-12-07|website=www.efloras.org}}</ref>

A common source of [[psyllium]], [[grind|ground]] psyllium seed husks are indigestible, providing a source of soluble [[dietary fiber]] which may be fermented into [[butyric acid]] – a [[short-chain fatty acid]] – by [[Butyric acid#Biosynthesis|butyrate-producing bacteria]].<ref name="Jov">{{cite journal |display-authors=3| last1=Jovanovski | first1=Elena | last2=Yashpal | first2=Shahen | last3=Komishon | first3=Allison | last4=Zurbau | first4=Andreea | last5=Blanco Mejia | first5=Sonia | last6=Ho | first6=Hoang Vi Thanh | last7=Li | first7=Dandan | last8=Sievenpiper | first8=John | last9=Duvnjak | first9=Lea | last10=Vuksan | first10=Vladimir | title=Effect of psyllium (''Plantago ovata'') fiber on LDL cholesterol and alternative lipid targets, non-HDL cholesterol and apolipoprotein B: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials | journal=The American Journal of Clinical Nutrition | volume=108 | issue=5 | date=15 September 2018 | issn=0002-9165 | doi=10.1093/ajcn/nqy115 | pages=922–932|pmid=30239559| doi-access=free }}</ref>  ''Plantago ovata'' is commonly used for commercial products containing psyllium.<ref>{{Cite book |editor-last=Melton |editor-first=Laurence |title=Encyclopedia of Food Chemistry |publisher=Elsevier |year=2019 |isbn=978-0-12-814045-1 |location=Netherlands |page=62 |language=en}}</ref>
